title: feat(plugin-markdown): ADR-0046 — heading anchors, code highlighting, GitHub alerts
body:
## Summary

Markdown **grammar v1.1** for the shared `@object-ui/plugin-markdown` renderer (used by docs + AI chat), implementing the agreed Tier 1 + Tier 2 enrichments from the ADR-0046 follow-up discussion. All three run **behind the existing `rehype-sanitize` gate**, which stays last in the chain as the final XSS boundary.

- **Heading anchors** (`rehype-slug` + `rehype-autolink-headings`) — headings get slug ids so intra-doc `#section` links resolve. This fixes a latent correctness gap: ADR-0046's own cross-reference design (`./doc.md#section`) had no anchor target at render time. `clobberPrefix: ''` keeps ids verbatim so author-written `#section` matches.
- **Code highlighting** (`rehype-highlight`) — fenced code blocks get highlight.js token classes; colors are theme-aware (light/dark) via an injected stylesheet built on the console's shadcn CSS variables. The audience for plugin/driver docs is developers, so this is the highest-value addition.
- **GitHub-style alerts** (`remark-github-blockquote-alert`) — `> [!NOTE]` / `[!TIP]` / `[!IMPORTANT]` / `[!WARNING]` / `[!CAUTION]` render as styled callouts. The syntax is valid CommonMark, so it **also renders natively in GitHub previews** (matching the ADR's "links just work on GitHub" philosophy) and degrades to a plain blockquote in any older renderer — **no CLI-lint coordination needed**.

### Why no lint change (correction to earlier framing)
The `> [!NOTE]` GFM-alert syntax is already a valid CommonMark blockquote, so the framework `os build` lint already accepts it and there is no broken-state risk. The lockstep concern only applies to `:::`-directive admonitions, which we did **not** choose. This PR is therefore renderer-only.

### Security posture (unchanged)
The sanitize schema is widened only for **inert** surfaces: `className`/`id` on `*`, `span`/`div` tags, and the autolink `<a>`. Class names and ids cannot execute code; `script` / `style` / event handlers / `javascript:` href / `iframe`/`object`/`embed` stay blocked. The alert icon **SVG is stripped** (svg is not whitelisted) — callout icons are CSS pseudo-elements, so there is **zero SVG surface** in the schema. A `class → className` canonicalization step runs before sanitize so the alert plugin's raw `class` attribute survives the whitelist.

### Deferred (Tier 3)
Mermaid and KaTeX are intentionally **not** included — per the discussion, Mermaid's real demand is served by ADR-0046 §3.5 live metadata rendering (flows/state-machines are metadata, not hand-drawn), and KaTeX has near-zero demand in business-app docs.

## Test plan
- [x] 10 new SSR render + security-regression cases (`markdown-render.test.tsx`): slug ids, verbatim anchors, highlight token classes surviving sanitize, alert callouts, GFM tables/tasks; and guards that `<script>`, `javascript:`, `onerror`, and the alert `<svg>` are all stripped
- [x] Existing registry tests still pass (15 total)
- [x] `vite build` (incl. dts) succeeds
